newsitem.title: CANADA: Transwest puts itself on the block.
newsitem.headline: Transwest puts itself on the block.

text.p: Transwest Energy Inc, which has an interest in the much-watched Moose Mountain oil and gas discovery in Alberta's Kananaskis Country, said on Tuesday it formed a directors committee and hired financial advisers to consider a merger or sale.
Transwest said it retained RBC Dominion Securities Inc as financial adviser.
The company has in place a shareholder rights plan that includes a "permitted bid" period of 90 days to allow its directors more time to consider unsolicited takeover bids.
Earlier this month, Don West, chief executive of Rigel Energy Corp, said Moose Mountain could come on stream as early as next spring.
Rigel holds one third working interest in the play and Husky Oil Ltd has the remainder. Transwest has a three percent overriding royalty on Rigel's stake.

The discovery, made three and a half years ago in a craggy, environmentally sensitive area of southwestern Alberta, has faced numerous delays in development because of the mountainous terrain, ecological concerns and opposition from environmental groups.
To date, five wells have been drilled on three pads at a cost of C$2 million to C$3 million each. Four hit oil and one hit natural gas. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
